To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

tRNA loci are the source of multiple RNA species that are able to execute a wide range of biological functions, including regulation of gene expression, translation and post-translational protein modification, RNA processing, and even RNA interference.
tRNA transcripts have a wide range of functions, including the modulation of gene expression and the regulation of protein synthesis.

(a) tRNAs are the most abundant RNA molecules in the cell; (b) they are involved in many cellular processes, including protein synthesis; (c) they can be found in various cellular compartments; (d) they can be modified by various enzymes; and (e) they can be processed to yield functional RNAs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular mechanisms that control tRNA transcription and processing.
the study of RNA biology and, more specifically, with the study of the functional roles of non-protein-coding transcripts, which are derived from non-protein-codifying genes.
the study of the mechanisms that regulate tRNA expression, and their impact in the cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tRNA transcriptome is much more complex than we have previously anticipated.
every little piece counts.
tRNA-derived RNAs (tdRNAs) are not only a new class of RNAs but a new class of RNA molecules, which is not surprising considering that tRNAs are the most abundant RNA molecules in all cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tRNA-derived RNA species can act as regulators or as effectors of biological processes.
tRNA-derived RNA molecules are not only the product of a random degradation process but rather the result of a highly regulated and controlled mechanism.
the tRNA transcriptome is a rich source of regulatory RNAs, whose functions range from transcription to translation, and even post-translation, as well as the regulation of the cell cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that

tRNA transcripts, in addition to their canonical function, may be used for multiple purposes, such as the modulation of gene expression, the regulation of chromatin, the modulation of the epigenome and the regulation of the transcriptome.
tRNA transcripts, which were previously thought to be a mere by-product of tRNA biosynthesis, are now considered to be an important source of functional non-coding RNAs.
, in addition to being a source of functional RNAs with a plethora of biological roles, tRNAs are also a source of regulatory RNAs.
